Strait of Hormuz Status: October 4, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  218 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
4 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.25 -0.11 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 WSJ reports oil was briefly moving through the Strait of Hormuz again before shipping attacks resurged; that report has not been independently confirmed in this feed.

02 Al Jazeera reports Iran says the strait will remain closed until the US meets seven conditions, while thenationalnews.com reports Iraq is shipping its oil through the Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran war chokes exports.

03 Middle East Eye, citing UKMTO, reports a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz; the October 2 attack involved an as-yet unidentified assailant.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the central flashpoint in the US-Iran confrontation, with the physical transit picture contested and attack pressure continuing. WSJ reports that oil was moving through the waterway again before shipping attacks resurged, though that report has not been independently confirmed in this feed. Al Jazeera reports Iran insists the strait will stay closed until the US meets seven conditions, with Iran's top negotiator stating the era of wasting time and dictating demands is over; separately, thenationalnews.com reports Iraq is shipping its oil through the strait even as the US-Iran war chokes exports, a counter-signal to the closure declaration. The site's carrier posture remains a cautious closed, but the physical transit picture is contested and neither claim should be read as settled. IMF PortWatch data for 2026-09-27 recorded 1 vessel transiting, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Al Arabiya English reports a tanker was damaged after an attack in the strait; Middle East Eye, citing UKMTO, reports a separate tanker was struck by an unknown projectile on October 2, with the attacker unidentified. Brent crude stood at $102.25 as of 17:57 UTC, down 0.11% in the last session before the close; futures are shut and that figure is unchanged since close. Seventy-two events were indexed in the past 24 hours. As of 17:50 UTC, 218 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
